requirement:
After applying a round's additions, Habeas MUST check freshness against the
edited sources. It MUST reassess a subject whose corrections are all satisfied
when the writes changed its assessment inputs. It MUST also reassess any other
subject whose previously current evidence those writes made stale, including
definitions, citation reviews, and site reviews outside the initial selection.
Independent reassessments MUST run under {cite}`requirements.authoring.concurrency`.
Each reassessment MUST use fresh inputs and the selected assessment policy.
Only a fresh successful assessment establishes `true`.

A subject with a remaining manual instruction or an action that could not be applied MUST pause for
the rest of the invocation, even if another edit changes its inputs. Other
subjects MUST continue. An already-present marker or stale selector alone MUST
cause no reassessment. If every requested marker already exists and the inputs
are unchanged, the negative judgment stands. Repeat while eligible subjects
remain, with no limit on rounds or automated additions. With `--stdout`, Habeas
MUST report the named subject's assessment and proposed corrections without
editing sources or starting a correction-driven reassessment.
rationale:
I found no unacknowledged test-adequacy gap. Each obligation in `requirements.authoring.reassessment` maps to a marked test with assertions.

- **Reassess a subject whose corrections are all satisfied, after the writes changed its inputs, with fresh inputs and the selected policy.**
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[corrections_replay_reference_only_mixed_and_regression_findings]` has a "reference-only" case. It adds markers, reassesses, fails again, adds a second marker, reassesses and succeeds. It checks the exact edited source text and `determination == true`.
  - Its "confirm-reassessment" case uses `--policy confirm`. It asserts four model requests, so the reassessment follows the selected policy.
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_collects_all_shared_file_findings_before_editing]` asserts that every retry request sees the edited source, and that each marker appears exactly once.
- **Only a fresh successful assessment gives `true`.** The "already present after reassessment" case ends with `determination == false`. The "mixed" and "inapplicable and valid" cases also end `false`.
- **Reassess other subjects whose current evidence became stale, outside the initial selection.**
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[reference_edits_reassess_a_skipped_subject_sharing_the_changed_input]` covers a requirement declaration review and a site review. It asserts that `src/lib.rs fn[shared]` and `requirement requirements.alpha` are reassessed after the edit.
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[a_named_reference_edit_refreshes_a_definition_and_a_citation_that_read_the_same_text]` covers a citation review. It asserts that `notes.txt <root>` and the other declaration reviews are rerun.
  - I read "definitions" as requirement or example declaration reviews. A `{definition}` can never be a subject, because it is never a reference target.
- **Independent reassessments run under concurrency.** `batch_collects_all_shared_file_findings_before_editing` measures the overlap of requests in the post-edit round separately. It asserts a peak of 2 with `concurrency = 2` over four peers, so the cap is both reached and respected.
- **A subject with a manual instruction or an unapplied action pauses for the rest of the invocation, and other subjects continue.**
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[a_changed_shared_input_does_not_resume_a_paused_subject]` covers both the manual-instruction pause and the unreachable-action pause. It asserts that `alpha` is requested twice and stays `false`, while `beta` is requested three times and ends `true`.
  - The "mixed", "inapplicable and valid" and "new-regression" cases in the replay test assert the pause messages.
- **An already-present marker or stale selector alone causes no reassessment, and the negative judgment stands.**
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stale_and_already_present_references_do_not_retry_unchanged_inputs]` covers both the stale and the already-present variants. It asserts that exactly two requests are made, that the source is unchanged or only the external edit remains, and that `determination` is `false`.
  - The replay test's "anchor" and "already present after reassessment" cases assert the "paused; requested markers already present, no assessment inputs changed" line.
- **Repeat while eligible subjects remain.** The "reference-only" case runs two correction rounds. The batch test runs initial and retry rounds.
- **`--stdout` reports the assessment and proposed corrections without editing sources or starting a reassessment.** The "stdout" case asserts that the evidence file is unchanged, that the output carries the proposed correction, that no "(applied)" appears, and that the source has 0 markers and exactly the original requests.

After applying a round's additions, Habeas MUST check freshness against the
edited sources. It MUST reassess a subject whose corrections are all satisfied
when the writes changed its assessment inputs. It MUST also reassess any other
subject whose previously current evidence those writes made stale, including
definitions, citation reviews, and site reviews outside the initial selection.
Independent reassessments MUST run under {cite}`requirements.authoring.concurrency`.
Each reassessment MUST use fresh inputs and the selected assessment policy.
Only a fresh successful assessment establishes `true`.
A subject with a remaining manual instruction or an action that could not be applied MUST pause for
the rest of the invocation, even if another edit changes its inputs. Other
subjects MUST continue. An already-present marker or stale selector alone MUST
cause no reassessment. If every requested marker already exists and the inputs
are unchanged, the negative judgment stands. Repeat while eligible subjects
remain, with no limit on rounds or automated additions. With `--stdout`, Habeas
MUST report the named subject's assessment and proposed corrections without
editing sources or starting a correction-driven reassessment.
:::{req} concurrency
Each named authoring configuration MUST accept an optional positive integer
`concurrency` in its configuration table. When omitted, the maximum number of
simultaneous assessments MUST default to the number of available logical CPUs
for Bedrock and OpenAI, falling back to one when that count is unavailable, and to one for
Ollama. A configured value MUST override the default for each backend; zero
MUST be rejected as invalid configuration.
Batch authoring MUST use asynchronous tasks on a runtime with a fixed worker
thread pool. The number of assessments running at once MUST NOT exceed the
selected concurrency. Each assessment MUST retain its own model conversation and
usage record. Transient provider failures, including throttling, MUST be
retried within the affected assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff`; every other provider error MUST
be reported through the ordinary assessment-failure path.
